slides.title: Sharing is dividing
slides.text: A sack of plums lands on the workbench and four friends are waiting. Sharing it fairly, so everyone gets the same, is division.

slides.title: Two sharing questions
slides.text: Division answers two questions. How many in each share, if you know the groups? Or how many groups, if you know the share size?

visual.label: Sharing in one strip: 29 plums, 4 friends, 7 each, 1 left over

focus.cue: Each friend gets 7, and 1 plum is left over.

slides.title: Rough first, then share
slides.text: Rough first: 29 plums shared by 4 friends is about 7 each. Share them out one by one and see what is left.

visual.label: 29 plums shared by 4 friends: 4 rows of 7, with 1 plum left over

focus.cue: One row for each friend: 7 plums each.
After fair shares of 7, 1 plum is left over.

slides.title: Leftovers need a decision
slides.text: A remainder is not a mistake. It is a leftover that needs a decision: one more van, a shared last slice, or a plum saved for later.

slides.title: Stretch: Big shares
slides.text: Long sharing works in chunks. For 96 shared by 4, share 80 first (20 each), then 16 (4 each). Each share is 24.

words.means: splitting an amount into equal shares or groups
one equal part that each person or group gets
what is left over after equal sharing
the answer to a division: how many in each share

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Sum Racer. It opens on the Sharing (division) track, division questions only, and it stays there. Win the race: picture the fair shares before you answer.
